violations.text: Bean sprouts were observed held at 49 degrees Fahrenheit. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Per interview with PIC, bean sprouts have been in unit since yesterday. See disposal. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 06/01/2026
No person in charge was present as needed at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 05/19/2026
The Person in charge did not assure compliance with critical code requirements. New Violation. Correct By: 05/19/2026

1) Raw animal foods (beef) were observed stored above ready-to-eat foods (cucumbers) in the walk-in refrigerator. Raw animal foods must be separated from raw ready-to-eat food such as vegetables during storage. 2) Raw animal foods were not stored properly to prevent cross-contamination. Raw chicken was observed stored above raw pork in the walk-in refrigerator. Except when combined as ingredients, different types of raw animal foods must be separated from each other during storage by using separate equipment or arranging each type of food in equipment so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented. Corrected On-Site. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 05/19/2026

Food contact surfaces of equipment/utensils (can opener) were observed with an accumulation of food and debris. The food contact surfaces of equipment must be clean to sight and touch. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 05/19/2026

The food-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils were not sanitized. The required utensil surface temperature of 160 degrees Fahrenheit was not achieved during the sanitizing cycle of the dishwasher as evidenced by the failure of the thermolabel (temperature indicator) affixed to the surface of a utensil to turn black. Establishment to sanitize in three bay sink until serviced. Service was called at time of inspection. New Violation. Correct By: 05/19/2026

Soup was observed held at 99 degrees Fahrenheit. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be maintained at 135 degrees Fahrenheit or above except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Soup was reheated at time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 05/19/2026

1) Garlic was observed held out of temperature control at 71 degrees Fahrenheit. Garlic was placed in ice bath at time of inspection. 2) Bean sprouts and eggs were observed held at 51-61 degrees Fahrenheit. See disposal. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. New Violation. Correct By: 05/19/2026

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. At time of inspection, chicken fingers were placed hot in the refrigerator in containers greater than four inches deep. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 05/19/2026
Chicken was observed stored on the floor in the walk-in cooler. Food must be stored at least 6 inches above the floor. New Violation. Correct By: 05/19/2026

1) Utensils were observed stored in stagnant water between uses. 2) Knives were stored on an unclean surface (in between table and prep unit) between uses. During pauses in food preparation, utensils must be stored on a clean surface or in a clean, protected location. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 05/19/2026

Prep unit #1 was not in good repair, ambient observed at 44 degrees Fahrenheit. Unit was taken out of service at time of inspection. TCS foods not be to held in unit until serviced and has an ambient temperature of 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below. New Violation. Correct By: 06/02/2026
The non-food contact surfaces of the following have an accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. 1) Shelving throughout kitchen 2) Vents New Violation. Correct By: 06/02/2026
At time of inspection, three bay sink at the bar was lacking hot water, faucet was not operable. New Violation. Correct By: 06/02/2026

1) The wall in the warewashing area (main kitchen) has an accumulation of black residue.2) The floors and walls throughout the facility have an accumulation of soil residue and/or food debris. The physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. New Violation. Correct By: 06/02/2026

Raw animal foods (such as beef) were observed stored above ready-to-eat foods (such as carrots) in the walk-in refrigerator. Raw animal foods must be separated from raw ready-to-eat food such as carrots during storage. Corrected On-Site. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 02/20/2025
A container was observed in the sushi bar hand-washing sink. A hand-washing sink must not be used for purposes other than hand washing. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 02/20/2025

Raw animal foods (such as shrimp) were observed stored above ready-to-eat foods (such as cucumbers) in the walk-in refrigerator. Raw animal foods must be separated from raw ready-to-eat food such as vegetables during storage. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 02/20/2025

Food contact surfaces of equipment/utensils (ice machine) were observed with an accumulation of biofilm. The food contact surfaces of equipment must be clean to sight and touch. Ice was voluntarily disposed of (see attached disposal form). Ice machine was taken out of service and cleaned at time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 02/20/2025

The food-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils were not sanitized. The required utensil surface temperature of 160 degrees Fahrenheit was not achieved during the sanitizing cycle of the dishwasher as evidenced by the failure of the thermolabel (temperature indicator) affixed to the surface of a utensil to turn black. Dishwasher was taken out of service and must not be used until it is repaired. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 02/27/2025

The quaternary ammonium concentration in the sanitizing solution of the 3-bay sink was 100 parts per million (ppm). According to the manufacturer's use directions, the concentration of the quaternary ammonium must be 200-400 ppm. Establishment must discontinue using the quaternary ammonium dispenser until it is repaired/replaced/adjusted. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 02/27/2025

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Chicken and shrimp were placed hot in the refrigerator in containers greater than four inches deep. Both were relocated to a sheet pan to rapidly cool. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 02/20/2025

Thermometers are lacking in the refrigeration unit(s). Cold holding equipment used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods must have at least one thermometer that is located to allow easy viewing of the temperature display. New Violation. Correct By: 02/27/2025

Food was observed stored on the floor in the walk-in cooler, walk-in freezer, and on the basement floor. Food must be stored at least 6 inches above the floor. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 02/20/2025

Knives are stored on an unclean surface (between prep units) between uses. During pauses in food preparation, utensils must be stored on a clean surface or in a clean, protected location. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 02/20/2025

Raw animal foods (such as shrimp) were observed stored above ready-to-eat foods (such as chicken) in the 2 door refrigerator. Raw animal foods must be separated from raw ready-to-eat food such as vegetables during storage. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 12/18/2023

The food-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils were not sanitized. The required utensil surface temperature of 160 degrees Fahrenheit was not achieved during the sanitizing cycle of the dishwasher as evidenced by the failure of the thermolabel (temperature indicator) affixed to the surface of a utensil to turn black. Unit to be taken out of service until it can be repaired/replaced/serviced. New Violation. Correct By: 12/18/2023

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Chicken and shrimp was placed hot in the refrigerator in containers greater than four inches deep. Items moved to sheet pan to properly cool. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 12/18/2023

Working containers of dry ingredients are not labeled with the common name of the food. Working containers holding food or food ingredients that are removed from their original packages, such as flour, herbs, salt, sugar, and spices must be labeled with the common name of the food. New Violation. Correct By: 12/18/2023

The door to the outside, located in the dining room, is not tight-fitting. Outer openings of a food establishment must be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by tight-fitting doors. New Violation. Correct By: 01/01/2024
Knives were observed stored in-between in the prep units at the cookline. PIC removed items from cookline and moved to warewashing area. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 12/18/2023
The non-food contact surfaces of the fan that is used in the prep area and the ice machine has an accumulation of dust and biofilm. New Violation. Correct By: 12/18/2023
The floors in the dry storage areas has an accumulation of rodent droppings. The physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. New Violation. Correct By: 12/18/2023
